method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)' (ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026), 18 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that "eviQ content should not be hosted on external sites", and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright, last updated 16 February 2022)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032) 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer' (published online 28 January 2026), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12947637). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every eviQ olaparib claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the ESMO 2026 Express Update to the 2023 ESMO epithelial ovarian cancer guideline (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, paraphrased), for first-line PARP inhibitor choice by BRCA and HRD status (including niraparib, rucaparib and olaparib with bevacizumab), maintenance after relapse, and mirvetuximab for platinum-resistant disease. The full ESMO 2023 guideline (Annals of Oncology) is not on Europe PMC; the Pan-Asia adapted ESMO 2025 guideline (PMC12180976) was read but not used because the 2026 Express Update is newer.

claims.claim: **First-line maintenance:** olaparib is for BRCA-mutated (germline or somatic), FIGO stage III or IV, high-grade serous cancer of the ovary, fallopian tube or peritoneum that has responded, completely or partially, to first-line platinum chemotherapy.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-line duration:** stop at 2 years if there is a complete response (no disease on imaging). If disease is still visible but stable at 2 years, the clinician may continue when further benefit is expected.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance after relapse:** for BRCA-mutated high-grade serous disease that relapsed but stayed platinum-sensitive and is responding after at least two platinum-containing regimens. No data support giving olaparib maintenance again after a later relapse.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wait for blood counts to recover** from earlier chemotherapy before starting olaparib.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Olaparib tablets 300 mg (2 × 150 mg) by mouth twice daily**, continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity; taking it with food can reduce nausea. PBS authority; 100 mg and 150 mg tablets.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Metoclopramide 10 mg as needed** (no more than 30 mg in 24 hours, for up to 5 days) is supplied at the start. Nausea can be moderate in the first month or months but usually settles with antiemetics and reassurance, without dose changes.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose steps for blood toxicity go 300, then 250, then 200 mg twice daily, then stop.** For ANC under 1.0 or platelets under 75, delay until recovery; the first episode restarts at 300 mg and each later one a step lower. For grade 3 or 4 anaemia, delay until haemoglobin is above 9 g/dL.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney:** with eGFR 31 to 50, reduce to 200 mg twice daily and monitor; it has not been studied below 30. **Liver:** no change for mild or moderate impairment; not recommended in severe impairment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **MDS and AML:** PARP inhibitors may increase the risk of myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, so check a full blood count with film regularly. Do not give olaparib to anyone with a history of bone marrow dysplasia.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** LFTs, FBC and EUC/eGFR at baseline, monthly through the first year, then as indicated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pneumonitis, occasionally fatal:** with new or worsening breathlessness, cough, fever or a radiological abnormality, withhold olaparib and investigate promptly; stop it if pneumonitis is confirmed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wound healing:** pause olaparib around major surgery and restart once healing is judged adequate.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fatigue** is common early and usually eases. Exclude other causes and advise graded exercise; if it stays severe despite breaks, consider a short interruption or a lower dose.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis B screening is not routinely needed** but can be considered in high-risk people. The safety of live vaccines during and after olaparib is not established.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **PARP inhibitor maintenance, with or without bevacizumab, is recommended for BRCA1/2-mutated or BRCA-wild-type HRD-positive cancer** that has no evidence of disease, or a complete or partial response, after first-line platinum and paclitaxel [I, A].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **BRCA1/2-mutated, in ESMO's order:** olaparib for 2 years (ESMO-MCBS 4); olaparib for 2 years with bevacizumab for 15 months (3); rucaparib for 2 years (3); niraparib for 3 years (2). **BRCA-wild-type, HRD-positive:** rucaparib for 2 years (3), niraparib for 3 years (2), or olaparib 2 years with bevacizumab 15 months (1).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **HRD-negative tumours:** options are 15 months of bevacizumab [I, A], 2 years of rucaparib [I, B] or 3 years of niraparib [I, B], the last two only after a response or with no evidence of disease. Choose by disease distribution, response to chemotherapy and the patient's characteristics.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No response to platinum means no PARP inhibitor:** use bevacizumab maintenance if appropriate (mainly for stable disease), or second-line treatment for progression. For frail patients, weekly paclitaxel 60 mg/m² with weekly carboplatin AUC 2 is an alternative [I, B].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **New first-line evidence (ATHENA-MONO, rucaparib):** median PFS 28.7 against 11.3 months in HRD-positive disease (HR 0.47), 20.2 against 9.2 months overall (HR 0.52), and 12.1 against 9.1 months even in HRD-negative disease (HR 0.65); overall survival was immature. Grade 3 or worse anaemia occurred in 28.7% and neutropenia in 14.6%, and MDS or AML in 0.5%.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Platinum-free interval guides treatment at relapse:** response and PFS are lower when it is under 6 months, and patients progressing on platinum, or soon after it, should get non-platinum treatment. **Maintenance after response to platinum at relapse** continues until progression or the next line [I, A]: olaparib for BRCA1/2-mutated disease, niraparib or rucaparib whatever the BRCA status.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **When platinum is not an option,** non-platinum chemotherapy (weekly paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, topotecan) gives low response rates (30–35% for weekly paclitaxel) and no clear survival gain; adding bevacizumab improves PFS and response but not OS.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mirvetuximab soravtansine is recommended for high-grade serous cancer with a platinum-free interval under 6 months and high folate receptor alpha expression (at least 75% of tumour cells staining 2+ or 3+), after one to three prior lines** [I, A; ESMO-MCBS 3]. In MIRASOL (453 patients) it improved median OS to 16.46 from 12.75 months (HR 0.67) and response to 42.3% from 15.9%.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mirvetuximab eye toxicity:** ocular events affected 56.0% (blurred vision, keratopathy) but were mostly low-grade and reversible, and only 1.8% stopped because of them. Use lubricating artificial tears and regular eye examinations.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); Gonzalez-Martin A, Ledermann J, ESMO Open (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2025.106032), 'ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline Express Update on the management of epithelial ovarian cancer', published online 28 January 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12947637/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **SOLO1 (first-line maintenance, 391 BRCA-mutated patients):** after 5 years' follow-up, median PFS was 56.0 months with olaparib against 13.8 months with placebo (HR 0.33), and 48.3% against 20.5% were free of progression at 5 years.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SOLO1 at 7 years:** 67.0% were alive with olaparib against 46.5% with placebo (HR 0.55). The gain is clinically meaningful but missed the trial's prespecified significance threshold.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SOLO2 (platinum-sensitive relapse, 295 BRCA-mutated patients):** median PFS 19.1 against 5.5 months (HR 0.30). At final analysis, median overall survival was 51.7 against 38.8 months (HR 0.74, p=0.054).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Harms in SOLO2:** grade 3 to 4 anaemia in 21% on olaparib. Treatment-emergent events led to interruption in 50%, dose reduction in 28% and stopping in 17%, and 5 patients (3%) died of treatment-related MDS or AML.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Advanced, metastatic or recurrent olaparib (eviQ ID 3737 v.7)', ID 3737 v.7; first approved 15 December 2020, last reviewed 2 September 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3737, retrieved 2026-09-23
